concepts.def: Core vocabulary: mis padres, mi hermano mayor (older brother), mis abuelos, mi mejor amigo (best friend), los primos (cousins).
Describe people with ser plus adjectives: 'Mi madre es alta y simpática'; adjectives agree in gender and number.
Spanish uses tener for age and features: 'Tengo quince años', 'Tiene el pelo castaño y los ojos verdes'.
Home vocabulary: vivo en un piso (flat) o una casa; las habitaciones include la cocina, el salón, el dormitorio y el cuarto de baño.
Social plans: quedar con amigos (to meet up), '¿Quieres salir el sábado?', ir al cine, dar una vuelta.
Possessives agree in number: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus - 'mis hermanos' (my brothers), 'su hermana' (his, her or their sister).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area B: Personal and Social Life — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area B: Personal and Social Life brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area B: Personal and Social Life.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am fifteen years old' in Spanish?
options: Tengo quince años
Soy quince años
Estoy quince años
Hago quince años

mcqs.q: 'Su hermana' can mean which of the following?
options: His, her or their sister
Only 'his sister'
My sister
Your (informal) sister

mcqs.q: Which sentence shows correct adjective agreement?
options: Mi madre es simpática
Mi madre es simpático
Mi madre es simpáticos
Mi madre es simpáticas

mcqs.q: 'El dormitorio' is which room of the house?
options: The bedroom
The kitchen
The bathroom
The dining room

mcqs.q: How do you say your age in Spanish?
options: With tener: 'Tengo quince años' - literally 'I have fifteen years'.
With hacer: 'Hago quince años'.
Sporty.
With ser, copying English: 'Soy quince años'.
Su always translates as 'his'.
With hacer: 'Hago quince años'.
No - 'su' can mean his, her, its, their, or formal your; context decides.
Su means 'our'.

mcqs.q: What does 'simpático' mean when describing a friend?
options: Nice or friendly.
Sympathetic, because the words look alike.
Sporty.
With hacer: 'Hago quince años'.
